Hi Lena — thanks for the clear list. Confirming receipt of evaluation_sample_subset.csv and answers below; Dev will follow with a short SDK/cURL snippet and a proposed tuning sweep config.

1) Endpoint model
We expose a scoring endpoint (POST /v1/rerank) that accepts: query (text or embedding), list of candidate ids or candidate embeddings (up to ~1000), and optional context/tool-call metadata. Response is a ranked list with scores. You can send either raw embeddings or let Redwood compute embeddings — both supported.

Request params (short):
- query_embedding OR query_text
- candidates: array of {id, text, embedding?}
- candidate_embeddings: boolean (if you provide embeddings)
- top_k: integer (how many results to return)
- score_only: boolean (if true, returns scores without reordering on server)

2) top_k semantics / candidate pool
- "top_k" in the rerank endpoint is the number of items returned to the application. The reranker typically scores the full candidate pool you send. For best results we recommend:
  - Candidate generation size: 200-500 for most search use-cases. This gives a good recall budget while keeping scoring latency reasonable.
  - Start your eval with candidate_pool=500 and top_k sweep [1,3,5,10] to understand how business metrics move as you reduce final result set.

3) Evaluation metrics we recommend
- Recall@k (candidate generation): ensure candidate pool contains the gold item >=95% of the time.
- NDCG@k and MRR (ranking quality): primary ranking metrics; report NDCG@5 and MRR.
- Recall@100 / Recall@500: useful for diagnosing candidate generator coverage.
- Precision@k if you have binary relevance labels.
- For production gates we typically look for: NDCG@5 > 0.45 (domain dependent) and stable MRR improvements over baseline retrieval. We'll surface recommended targets after we run your sample.

4) Embedding model compatibility
- The reranker is trained to be fairly robust to upstream embeddings, but quality improves when embedding encoder and reranker are aligned. If moving to a different embedding model is costly, you can run the baseline with your current ava-embed-3-small. If results are below expectations we can test our recommended embed-6b model for candidate generation as an A/B.

5) Latency expectations
- Baseline scoring latencies (P95) for scoring ~500 candidates vary by model size and quantization. Typical numbers on our dedicated nodes: 120-250ms P95 for a medium-sized reranker (7B quantized); 60-150ms for smaller reranker variants. We'll provide measured numbers when we run your sample. If you need sub-50ms P95 we'll discuss a hybrid approach (local lightweight reranker for top candidates + remote heavyweight for accuracy-sensitive requests).

Thanks Marissa / Lena — I ran a quick baseline on the 120-row sample you sent. High-level notes (more detailed CSV/report attached if helpful):

- Baseline config used: reranker-medium (quantized), candidate_pool=500 (we padded with similar docs), top_k=10 for evaluation.
- Results (quick): NDCG@5 = 0.42, MRR = 0.34, Recall@100 = 0.87.
- Observations: several failure cases where the gold item was not present in the candidate pool (candidate gen recall) — we should run a candidate model variation (your embedding vs embed-6b) to compare.
- Latency: measured P95 ~180ms for scoring 500 candidates on our dedicated test node.

Suggested next experiments
1) Candidate generator sweep: ava-embed-3-small vs redwood-embed-6b with candidate_pool sizes [200, 400, 600].
2) Reranker sweep: try reranker-small, reranker-medium, record NDCG@5/MRR and P95.
3) top_k analysis: evaluate downstream business metric sensitivity at top_k=[1,3,5,10].

SDK / example cURL (short):
POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/rerank
Content-Type: application/json
Body: {"query_embedding": [..], "candidates": [{"id":"cid1","text":"..."}], "top_k": 10}
